# Implement block: Mood Card Shuffle (Jetpack Compose)

You are adding the "Mood Card Shuffle" block from Native Cook to the user's Android app. The block already exists as working Kotlin code. Your job is to bring it into this project faithfully, not to write a new one that looks similar.

## The block

A mood-based place finder over a full-screen, softly blurred and muted copy of the front card's photo, with "Where do you feel like going?" set large and centred at the top. In the middle sits a deck of four landscape photo cards arranged like a drum: the front one upright and the next and previous ones peeking out on either side, smaller, darker and turned away in 3D. The front card carries a white "Curated" chip, a round bookmark button, a small-caps region line ("Yên Bái · Vietnam"), the place's name and a two-line blurb. A frosted "Search places…" pill sits under the deck, and a white sheet at the bottom holds the mood chips (Quiet, Nature, Artisanal Food, Wild) with a sliding black pill on the chosen one, and a "Go Unexpected" row with a round shuffle button. Swiping turns the deck: the front card swings out to the side and tucks in behind while the next one slides in over it and straightens up, and picking a mood riffles the deck into a pile and deals out a new set of places.

**Motion.** The deck and the backdrop are drawn in one canvas, every frame computed on the UI thread. A card's place is its signed distance s from the front (−2 … 2 cards) and its pose follows the angle s·90° around a drum: it moves out sideways by sin(angle) × 0.25 card widths, shrinks by 30%, drops 18 pt and darkens by up to 62% towards the back ((1 − cos angle)/2), turns up to 16° with its outer edge away and tilts 1.6°; each card is drawn through its own perspective matrix (vanishing point 900 pt away). The front card is 68% of the screen's width (at most 300 pt), 0.84 as tall, with 26 pt corners and a soft shadow (16 pt blur, 16 pt drop). The card leaving the front swings out the way the deck turns, up to 0.36 card widths further, 26° more, lifted 14 pt and shrunk 8% at the middle of its move (a sine arc), then tucks in as the peek, while the card arriving slides straight in over it; which card swings follows the deck's heading, eased over 0.12 s, so a reversal never jumps. Cards are drawn back to front; where two neighbours are within 0.3 of a card of trading places, the lower one is drawn again on top at up to 50% opacity, so every change of order is a cross-fade, never a cut. The chip, bookmark, text and the shade under them show only on the front card, fading out by a third of a card. Dragging turns the deck one card per 72% of the screen's width (left for the next card), with a rubber band (20%) past one card either way; on release the deck lands on a spring (mass 1, stiffness 90, damping 17) that carries the finger's speed, committing when the position projected 0.18 s ahead passes half a card, with a light haptic. Tapping a peeking card turns the deck to it on the same spring; tapping the bookmark fills it and pops it to 1.28× over 0.11 s and back on a damped wobble, with a light haptic. Each photo loads once (800 px) and fades in over 0.35 s; its backdrop is blurred once into a 120 × 260 px image (9 px blur, 72% saturation) drawn stretched over the screen, cross-fading between the two cards nearest the front in step with the deck. Choosing a mood moves the black pill on a spring (420 ms, damping ratio 0.82) and reshuffles over 1.15 s: the cards gather into a riffled pile (offset ±0.12 card widths, tilted ±7°, stepping up 10 pt each) over the first 36%, turn edge-on together between 44% and 56% while their faces change to the new mood, then turn back and deal out; the old backdrop fades out over 0.52 s, and a selection haptic marks the choice. "Go Unexpected" picks a random other mood. The self-playing demo (LOOP 14 s) turns a card at 1.0 s and 2.4 s on an ease-in-out curve (1.15 s, 0.5, 0, 0.25, 1), reshuffles to Nature at 3.8 s, turns a card at 5.6 s, reshuffles to Wild at 7.0 s, turns two cards at 8.8 s and 10.2 s and reshuffles back to Quiet at 11.6 s, ending on the deck it started with; a touch pauses it for 4 s. Under reduced motion nothing swings, spins or riffles: cards slide and cross-fade between places, and the deck dips out and back in while a reshuffle changes its faces.

## Reference source

The block is built and running in the Native Cook source repository. Each link below is a file on GitHub. To read one as plain text, replace `https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/` with `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/` in its address.

### Demo (start here)

- [MoodCardShuffleDemo.kt](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/kotlin/app/src/main/java/com/ngocdevv/nativecook/blocks/cards/moodcardshuffle/MoodCardShuffleDemo.kt)

### Files of the block

- [MoodCardShuffle.kt](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/kotlin/app/src/main/java/com/ngocdevv/nativecook/blocks/cards/moodcardshuffle/MoodCardShuffle.kt)
- [MoodCardShuffleEngine.kt](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/kotlin/app/src/main/java/com/ngocdevv/nativecook/blocks/cards/moodcardshuffle/MoodCardShuffleEngine.kt)
- [MoodCardShufflePainter.kt](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/kotlin/app/src/main/java/com/ngocdevv/nativecook/blocks/cards/moodcardshuffle/MoodCardShufflePainter.kt)

## Your instructions

_Anything specific to this app goes here: where the block should appear, what to rename, what to change. Left empty, integrate the block as it is._

## How to work

Work like an experienced Android engineer joining an existing project: learn the app first, read only what you need, decide early how the block fits, then integrate it with as little disruption as possible. Take the steps in order.

**Done means** the block is reachable in the user's app and behaves like the reference on an emulator or a device. A Compose preview is useful while you work, but it is not the proof: build, install and run the app.

**Fidelity.** Bring over the real implementation. Keep its structure, colours, sizes, timings and easing. Change only what this project requires and what "Your instructions" ask for.

If you already learned this project earlier in the conversation, reuse what you know and skip step 2. Learn it again only if the project changed or something you need is missing.

### 1. Check where you are

- You need the project's files and a terminal. If this prompt was pasted into a chat that has neither, stop and say so: it has to be run by a coding agent opened on the project.
- Confirm the project is an Android app built with Gradle. If it is something else, stop, say what you found, and do not create a new app inside it unless the instructions ask for one.

### 2. Learn the host app

- The app module, its namespace, `minSdk`, `compileSdk`, and the versions of Kotlin, the Android Gradle Plugin and Compose (a BOM or single versions).
- Whether Compose is switched on in that module, and whether screens are Compose, Views or both.
- Navigation: Navigation Compose, fragments, activities, or a single screen. Find how a screen is added today.
- How dependencies are declared: a version catalog (`libs.versions.toml`) or directly in `build.gradle`.
- Conventions: package layout, naming, theme, where resources live and how they are named.

### 3. Read the block

- Open the demo, then each file in the block's package. The list above names every file of the block, and the resources it uses from outside its package.
- The demo is how the source repository shows the block. Bring over what the demo shows, not the repository's gallery. Anything listed under "Used by the demo only" stays behind.
- Read the block's parameters and their defaults. The demo may switch on an option that makes the block play by itself for a recording (for example `autoPlay`). Keep the option; leave it off in the user's app unless asked.

### 4. Decide the fit

- Compare the block's libraries and the versions it was built with to the host's. Add what is missing the way this project declares dependencies. Do not upgrade the host's Kotlin, Gradle plugin or Compose versions without asking; if an API differs on the host's version, adapt the block's code.
- Check `minSdk`. If the block uses an API newer than the host's minimum, keep the fallback the source has, or tell the user what would be lost.
- If Compose is not switched on in the module, say what turning it on involves before you do it. In a View-based screen, show the block through a `ComposeView`.
- Shared helpers: copy the ones the block imports next to it, or fold them into the block's files. Do not copy helpers it never calls.

### 5. Bring it in

- Copy the block's files into a package of this app, and rewrite the `package` lines and the imports, including the import of the app's own `R` class.
- Copy its resources and asset files. Keep their names unless one collides with a resource of the app; then rename it everywhere it is used.
- Keep reduced-motion handling, haptics and accessibility descriptions as they are in the source. If the block needs a permission, add it to the manifest and say so.
- Mount the block where the instructions say. With no instructions, add a screen or destination named after the block and make it reachable the way the app's other screens are.

### 6. Run it

- Build with the project's own task, for example `./gradlew :app:assembleDebug`, and fix every error and new warning the block introduced.
- Install and run it, and use the block: every state, every gesture, and once with animations switched off in the system settings.
- If the build or the emulator fails for a reason outside the block, report the error and ask how to continue.

### 7. Report

- Files added and changed, dependencies and permissions added, and anything renamed to avoid a collision.
- How to reach the block in the app.
- Anything that differs from the reference, and why.
